title: FACIAL CLEFTING, OBLIQUE, 1
alt_titles: OCULOMAXILLOFACIAL DYSPLASIA WITH OBLIQUE FACIAL CLEFTS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that oblique facial clefting-1 (OBLFC1) is caused by mutation in the SPECC1L gene (614140) on chromosome 22q11.23.

checks.claim: Oblique facial clefting-1 (OBLFC1) is caused by mutation in the SPECC1L gene.
checks.evidence_quote: We show that loss-of-function mutations in SPECC1L are pathogenic for this human developmental disorder
checks.explanation: Abstract states loss-of-function SPECC1L mutations are pathogenic for oblique facial clefts; OBLFC1 designation is nomenclature.

checks.claim: The SPECC1L gene is located on chromosome 22q11.23.
checks.evidence_quote: Deficiency of the cytoskeletal protein SPECC1L leads to oblique facial clefting.
checks.explanation: The abstract does not give the chromosomal location. It counts as supported only because the rules treat a gene's location as standard nomenclature.

paragraphs.text: Oblique facial clefts are rare malformations (Dasouki et al., 1988). They include types 2 to 6 of Tessier's classification (Richieri-Costa and Gorlin, 1994). They can occur together with other malformations (Dasouki et al., 1988).

checks.claim: Oblique facial clefts are rare malformations.
checks.evidence_quote: Chromosomal studies should be performed in children with such rare malformations.
checks.explanation: The abstract calls oblique facial clefts rare malformations.

checks.claim: Oblique facial clefts include types 2 to 6 of Tessier's classification.
checks.evidence_quote: Oblique facial clefts are rare and include types 2-6 of Tessier's classification.

checks.claim: Oblique facial clefts can occur together with other malformations.
checks.evidence_quote: An eight month old girl was born with symmetrical bilateral oblique facial clefts and calcaneovarus foot deformity. CT scan of the head showed severe bilateral ocular hypoplasia
checks.explanation: In the case described, the clefts occurred with a foot deformity and ocular hypoplasia, so they can occur with other malformations.

paragraphs.text: Dasouki et al. (1988) described an 8-month-old girl who was born with symmetric bilateral oblique facial clefts and a calcaneovarus foot deformity. A CT scan of the head showed severe bilateral ocular hypoplasia.

checks.evidence_quote: An eight month old girl was born with symmetrical bilateral oblique facial clefts
checks.explanation: The abstract states the patient's age, sex and finding directly.

checks.evidence_quote: CT scan of the head showed severe bilateral ocular hypoplasia and normal brain parenchyma.

paragraphs.text: Saadi et al. (2011) showed that loss-of-function mutations in the SPECC1L gene are pathogenic for oblique facial clefting. Their functional studies supported a role for SPECC1L in craniofacial development. In zebrafish, knockdown of a SPECC1L homolog produced a 'faceless' phenotype, with loss of jaw and facial structures. In cultured cells, SPECC1L deficiency caused defective reorganization of the actin cytoskeleton and abnormal cell migration. Saadi et al. (2011) concluded that SPECC1L functions in actin-cytoskeleton reorganization and is required for proper facial morphogenesis.
